title: Metric Beacon: compatibility layer for divergent Prometheus/OTel inference KPIs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our Prometheus scrapers, OTLP collectors, and sidecars currently emit overlapping but inconsistent metric surfaces for the same inference events (e.g., token_latency_seconds vs. llm_inference_token_ms with different label sets). This makes reliable SLO calculation, per-tenant billing attribution, and latency/error dashboards brittle, especially across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. We also lack a deterministic way to attach span IDs and request-level tracing hooks to aggregated metric points for root-cause investigation.

Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility and reconciliation layer — Metric Beacon — that normalizes incoming Prometheus and OTLP metrics into a stable canonical envelope while preserving the original payload for debugging. Metric Beacon should: 1) produce canonical metric names and a fixed minimal label set for downstream SLO/alerting pipelines; 2) attach trace/span references and a request fingerprint to enable fast drilldowns; 3) support schema evolution with versioned mappings and transparent backfill; 4) emit conversion telemetry so we can monitor data-loss or drift during rollout.

Design overview: Metric Beacon sits as an ingest stage in the telemetry gateway (and as an optional sidecar for Private deployments). It performs three steps: 1) Classification - detect source (prometheus scrape, OTLP metrics, sidecar envelope) and metric family; 2) Canonicalization - map source metric and labels to canonical name/labels via a versioned mapping table; 3) Enrichment - stamp the envelope with: canonical_name, beacon_version, original_metric, original_labels_hash, request_fingerprint, trace_context if available. The canonical envelope is forwarded to existing downstream pipelines (OTLP router, Prometheus remote write adapter) alongside a copies stream to a debug retention tier.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (proof-of-concept, 2 weeks): implement Beacon as a standalone Go microservice with configuration-driven mapping rules and a small rule language. Add unit tests and fuzzer for label collisions. Phase 2 (integration, 3 weeks): integrate Beacon into telemetry gateway, wire canonical outputs to the current KPI aggregators and to an isolated debug topic. Add conversion telemetry (per-metric conversion rate, unmapped families). Phase 3 (rollout, 3 weeks): canary in staging, cross-region canary in hosted, opt-in for Dedicated, sidecar preview for Private. Provide backfill job to reprocess 7 days of raw debug stream where needed.

Operational requirements: Beacon must be horizontally scalable, have <5ms P95 processing overhead per metric family under typical batching, and expose Prometheus metrics for conversion success, rule hit counts, and labeled cardinality spikes. We will add circuit-breakers to bypass Beacon (pass-through) if memory or latency thresholds breach.

Dashboard and SLO work: Update latency/error dashboards to source canonical_name and request_fingerprint. Add a diagnostic panel that shows top unmapped metrics and top label churners per-tenant. Add an alert (P0) on conversion rate drop >5% for high-volume namespaces.

Backward compatibility and migration: Start with non-destructive mode where Beacon tags canonical_envelope but allows downstream to continue using original metrics. Gradually flip downstream consumers (SLO pipelines, billing attribution) to canonical_name. Maintain a migration log and a mapping UI in Console for observation and manual overrides.

Risks and mitigations: 1) Mapping errors causing SLO shifts — mitigate with shadow mode + backfill + canary. 2) High-cardinality explosion from enrichment — mitigate with sampling for debug stream and cardinality caps. 3) Security/privacy of original labels — redact tenant-sensitive labels and honor KMS-backed masking rules.

Deliverables: design doc link (drive/redwood-observability/metric-beacon-design), Beacon binary, gateway integration PR, a backfill job, dashboard updates, runbook, and a migration checklist.
